rationale: This is a mechanical stacking of three already-evaluated archive corners with no new economic content — and the nested SUMRANK silently weights the first corner 50% versus 25% each for the others, so any gain would be an artifact of arbitrary weighting rather than of the hypothesized "three independent traces."

A third two-corner recombination of components already in the archive (OperatingTighteningRegime and IndustryNeutralChronicAccrualDecay), and the two legs are not as orthogonal as claimed since low within-firm operating-capital intensity and low cumulative working-capital accrual are largely the same construct measured in level versus flow.

The second moment of accruals (Dechow-Dichev/Francis accrual quality) is genuinely absent from the archive, the interaction with sustained gross profitability is economically coherent, and the sign direction matches the expression — though the reviewer should watch that low accrual volatility × high gross profit does not collapse into a large-stable-firm profitability bet.

Adding a third conjunct to the best short corner repeats a pattern that already diluted results (TripleBloatDecayFragility: −3.6% vs the two-way −4.7%), and the claim that accrual volatility is "nearly uncorrelated with the accrual level" is mechanically dubious since the volatility of a scaled flow series rises with the magnitude of that flow.

The level-to-change repair is a legitimate, well-motivated way to strip the capital-intensity confound from a validated conservatism result, but the archive's own UnderDepreciationMarginGain (t = −0.22) suggests the ΔD&A leg carries little information, and rising dpc/at also picks up recent capex and impairment charges that cut against the conservatism story.

This is a recombination of existing corners rather than a new mechanism, but it is framed as a genuine ablation of the Soliman turnover confound that pervades every strong archive signal, and that diagnostic is worth running even though a null result would be as informative as a positive one.
